title: Do Not Commit to Anyone
summary: Law 20 advises remaining neutral and avoiding commitment to any side or faction. Committing to the powerful leads to being consumed, while siding with the weak wears you out. By staying unattached, offering promises without true obligation, and letting others compete for your favor, you maintain independence, gain intelligence, and profit regardless of the outcome.
example: Elizabeth I retained power and independence by keeping suitors and factions orbiting her without ever marrying or committing.
Henry Kissinger maintained influence by connecting with both sides and utilizing enemies' friends.
Queen Isabella appeared supportive while remaining neutral, preserving her realm while neighboring maps changed.
A ruler in Chinese history waited for two battling states to wear each other out before intervening to rescue one and capture the other.
Castruccio generated internal conflict to win control of a city.
George Washington politely declined short-term gains from France to build a stronger long-term foundation for America.
reversal: Making false promises repeatedly can expose your game, causing enemies to unite against you and resulting in a loss of trust and respect.
